title: Diagram creation fails from the ordinary entry point: projectId is URL-only state the UI never sets
description:
Creating a diagram from the ordinary entry point fails with:

  "Missing ?projectId= in the URL — create a project first (User Story 4)."

ROOT CAUSE
projectId is URL-only state that the application reads but never writes. Across all of
apps/web/src only two places touch it: the reader getProjectIdFromUrl() (App.tsx) and
AdminShell's back-link. Every <a href="?..."> in the app is an absolute query-string
replacement, so any click discards it. The only way to hold a projectId is to type it into the
address bar. App.tsx already carries a comment admitting the query param stands in for a project
chooser that was never built.

TWO JOURNEYS REACH IT
1. The ordinary entry point. Land on http://localhost:5173/ with no query string, sign in, click
   New Diagram, pick a type, click Create. This is not an edge case — it is what happens to
   anyone who does not know the parameter exists. Import Diagram and Create with AI fail the same
   way but at least fail on the first click.
2. In-app navigation drops it. home -> admin -> back loses the parameter on the FIRST hop.
   AdminShell's back-link is correct in isolation (it preserves what it is given); the loss is one
   hop earlier, in the ?admin= links that carry no projectId at all — five in AdminShell.tsx and
   five in App.tsx's home nav.

SECONDARY DEFECT
createDiagram() calls setPickingType(false) BEFORE the projectId guard, so the type-picker closes
and the user's chosen diagram type is discarded before the error is shown. Fixable in two lines
independently of the main fix.

WHY THE TEST SUITE NEVER CAUGHT IT — the part worth not re-learning
Every spec that clicks new-diagram, import-diagram-button or create-via-ai-chat first navigates
to /?projectId=${PROJECT_ID}. The only bare page.goto('/') calls are in accessibility.spec.ts
(login-page axe audit, never signs in) and ui-foundation.spec.ts (reads body/button styles, then
re-enters via a helper that supplies the parameter). No test ever reached the home screen without
it, so the defect was structurally invisible to a suite of 83 passing E2E tests. Test fixtures
that always supply a parameter the real UI never sets will hide this whole class of bug — prefer
at least one spec per entry point that navigates the way a user actually would.

OPTION EXPLICITLY REJECTED — do not revisit
"Fall back to the only/first project when the parameter is absent." It looks like the smallest
fix but is wrong: the projects table has no owner or membership column (0001_init.sql), so "the
user's project" is not expressible. The fallback would have to mean "the sole project" or "the
first project", which silently breaks the moment a second project exists, and there is no
GET /projects endpoint today anyway (only POST /projects, GET /projects/:id,
GET /projects/:id/tree).

Also rejected as a complete fix: threading projectId through the ten ?admin= links. It repairs
journey 2 only, leaves journey 1 broken, and makes the bug harder to hit — which is worse than
leaving it obvious.

EVIDENCE
apps/web/tests/e2e/project-context.spec.ts — three tests reproducing the real user journey rather
than hard-coding the parameter. Verified failing 0/3 for the right reasons before any fix:
app-error present where none expected (x2), and searchParams.get('projectId') null after an
admin round trip.
acceptance_criteria: A user landing on the app root with no query string can sign in and create, import, or AI-generate a diagram without touching the address bar. Project context survives navigation to an admin screen and back. The user's diagram-type choice is not discarded when creation cannot proceed. apps/web/tests/e2e/project-context.spec.ts passes without being weakened.
notes:
RESOLVED by feature 007 (branch 007-project-context).

Root cause as diagnosed: projectId was URL-only state the UI read but never wrote. Fixed by holding the selected project in application state, seeded from the address and written back with history.replaceState, plus a chooser in the shared header.

Planning uncovered a second, larger problem the bug report did not mention: NO route taking a project id checked anything beyond requireAuth, and getProjectTree read every project and every diagram in the installation with no predicate. Any signed-in user could read any project's whole diagram tree by id. Filtering only the chooser would have hidden project names from a dropdown while leaving them one request away, so server-side enforcement was added: requireProjectAccess on all five routes, projects.owner_id (migration 0006, backfilled), and GET /projects.

Verification: 154 diagram-core, 112 api (was 95), 96 E2E passed / 1 skipped / 0 failed (was 82 passed + 3 failed). The three reproduction tests in project-context.spec.ts pass with the file UNCHANGED (git diff empty) — SC-005.

Follow-up filed: canvas-ijq (diagram-only shares have no navigation path).
close_reason: Fixed in feature 007-project-context; reproduction tests pass unmodified.

title: Feature 004: AI-assisted diagram chat spec
description: specs/004-ai-diagram-chat/ - spec written, covers persona admin (create/edit/archive, tagged to architect category), create-via-chat, edit-via-chat (targeted tool-calling, not full regeneration), and per-diagram chat history persistence. Scoped to flowchart diagrams only for v1. Known prerequisite: diagram-core needs addNode/addEdge as pure functions (currently only removeNode/removeEdge/updateNodeLabel/updateEdgeLabel exist).
notes: Tasks generated (2026-07-26): specs/004-ai-diagram-chat/tasks.md, 33 tasks (T001-T033). Setup(2)+Foundational(7)+US1(12)+US2(3)+US3(5)+US4(2)+Polish(2). Unlike 003, stories genuinely build on each other (US2/3/4 each depend on artifacts US1 produces) - not mutually parallelizable across developers. Caught and fixed a real gap during tasks planning: added research.md decision #8 (AI SDK MockLanguageModelV1 test provider for both contract+E2E tests, real-provider smoke test is opt-in only via RUN_LIVE_AI_TESTS) - avoids CI needing live API keys. Next: /speckit-implement.

title: Feature 003: parser correctness fixes (comments everywhere, architecture arrowhead bug, ER attributes, sequence notes/blocks)
description: Next actionable slice of the Mermaid compliance roadmap, about to go through the spec-kit flow (specify/clarify/plan/tasks/implement) same as 001/002. Scope: (1) %% comment support in sequence/class/ER/C4/architecture parsers (flowchart already has it from feature 002); (2) fix architecture-beta parser's inability to parse arrowhead edges (-->, <--) at all — a real defect against documented syntax, not just a gap, and store the T/B/L/R direction hints it currently discards; (3) ER diagram attribute-block syntax (ENTITY { type name PK/FK/UK }) — currently unparseable, the single biggest real-world ER gap; (4) sequence diagram Note left/right/over (incl. multi-participant) and loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break blocks — currently only bare participant+message parses.
acceptance_criteria: A spec exists under specs/003-.../ following the same TDD-first constitution as 001/002; all 4 items have failing-then-passing contract tests; full regression suite green.
notes: Implementation complete (2026-07-26): all 19 tasks (T001-T019) done. Architecture -->/<-- arrowhead bug fixed, ER attribute blocks added, sequence notes+nestable control-flow blocks added (loop/alt/else/opt/par/and/critical/option/break), %% comments now honored in all 5 remaining parsers. Full regression: diagram-core 105/105, api 53/53, web E2E 29/29 (incl. opt-in perf). Zero apps/api changes; zero apps/web SOURCE changes (only 1 new E2E test) - confirmed the existing generic container rendering handles the new sequence notes/blocks with no frontend work needed. Manually verified via live API: architecture round-trip, ER attributes round-trip, deeply-nested alt-inside-loop with 3-participant note round-trips byte-for-byte, C4 comments, and the unclosed-ER-block structured error. Ready to close once user confirms.
close_reason: Merged to main via PR #3 (muirjc/canvas). All 4 user stories delivered, 19/19 tasks, CI green.

title: Flaky in CI: project-switch unsaved-changes confirmation sometimes never appears
description:
apps/web/tests/e2e/project-visibility.spec.ts has two tests covering the unsaved-changes warning on project switch. In GitHub Actions, ONE of them fails per run and it alternates which:
  run 30457177512 - 'confirming a project switch...' timed out on getByTestId('confirm-project-switch')
  run 30457608394 - 'switching project with unsaved changes warns...' failed on expect(project-switch-confirm).toBeVisible()
Both mean the confirmation dialog never rendered. Run 30468263191 then passed with no code change, confirming it is intermittent rather than fixed.

The dialog is skipped when any of these hold in App.tsx requestProjectChange: nextProjectId === projectId, diagram is null, or hasUnsavedChanges is false. hasUnsavedChanges is computed in DiagramEditor.tsx and reported to App through an onUnsavedChangesChange prop inside a useEffect.

NOT YET DIAGNOSED. Ruled out so far:
  - useDslSync does not debounce; dsl is a synchronous useMemo over model, so it is not serialization lag
  - both tests already wait for [data-testid^='node-'] to reach count 1, and in the CI failures that assertion PASSED and the next line failed, so the edit had landed
  - could not reproduce locally: tests in isolation (3x), whole spec file (3x), --repeat-each=4 (44/44), GET /projects delayed 2.5s so the list lands after the editor opens, and CDP CPU throttling at 20x
Untested difference: CI seeds a fresh database (seeded project has 0 diagrams) whereas the local dev DB has ~1114, and CI runs all 97 tests across all spec files in one worker.
design: Key question to answer first: is this a TEST defect or a genuine product race? If a real user can switch project and silently lose unsaved work, the fix belongs in App.tsx/DiagramEditor.tsx, not the test. The parent-mirrors-child-state design (child useEffect -> parent useState -> read during an event handler) is the fragile part and may be worth replacing regardless of the outcome.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified with evidence from a CI trace, and the two tests pass across at least 10 consecutive CI runs without any assertion being weakened.
notes: playwright.config.ts now sets trace: 'retain-on-failure', screenshot: 'only-on-failure' and enables the HTML reporter under CI, so the existing 'Upload Playwright report' step finally produces a usable artifact. The next occurrence will have a trace attached — start there. Do NOT fix by adding waitForTimeout or by relaxing the assertions: these tests exist because unsaved work must never be discarded silently (SC-006b).

title: A user with only a diagram-level share has no way to navigate to that diagram
description:
Feature 007 made project visibility access-controlled. A user who has been granted access to a single DIAGRAM, but not to its project, can no longer browse to it: the project browser needs project-level access, and there is no 'shared with me' list anywhere in the UI. The diagram is reachable only if someone sends them a direct link — and the editor has no per-diagram URL, so no such link exists.

Before 007 this worked, but only because any signed-in user could read any project's entire tree — i.e. the navigation path existed as a side effect of the access-control hole that 007 closed. Restoring the old behaviour is NOT the fix.

Surfaced by apps/web/tests/e2e/sharing.spec.ts, which navigates via the project browser to reach a diagram shared at view level. It passes today only because apps/api/src/seed/run.ts now also grants the architect project-level access to the seeded project — the seed masks the gap rather than the product solving it.
design: Two plausible directions: (a) a 'Shared with me' list on the home screen driven by share_grants where subject_type='diagram'; or (b) per-diagram deep links so a share can be delivered as a URL. (a) is self-contained; (b) is more broadly useful and would also let sharing.spec.ts navigate without any project grant.
acceptance_criteria: A user granted only a diagram-level share can reach and open that diagram through the UI, without holding any project-level access, and without being able to see any other diagram in that project.
notes:
INVESTIGATED 2026-07-29. Confirmed with a live probe (temporary user, one diagram-level 'view' grant, no project access):
  GET /projects              -> {"projects":[]}  (so the UI shows the 'no projects yet' invitation)
  GET /diagrams/<shared>     -> 200               (the diagram is ALREADY fully readable)
  GET /projects/<owner>/tree -> 403               (correctly refused)
Probe data removed afterwards; dev DB back to 2 users.

Conclusion: access control is correct and needs no change. The defect is purely DISCOVERY — plus an actively misleading empty state that tells a user they have nothing when work is waiting.

Correction to this issue's original DESIGN field: (a) and (b) are NOT alternatives. Per-diagram deep links do not fix this bug — the recipient still needs someone to send them a link, and nothing tells them there is anything to ask for. (b) is a worthwhile separate change; (a) is the fix.

New risk identified for the spec: a 'shared with me' row that names the owning project would breach feature 007's FR-013a ('projects belonging to others MUST NOT be listed or named') while looking helpful. Needs an explicit decision.

Also noted: apps/api/src/seed/run.ts grants the architect project-level access, so sharing.spec.ts passes via the project browser and NO test currently covers the diagram-only case.

Brief prepared at docs/shared-diagram-access-brief.md. Routing through the full speckit cycle as feature 008.

title: AI-assisted diagram chat (persona-driven natural language creation/editing)
description: New initiative: bring AI capabilities into the platform via a persona-driven chat interface (Vercel AI SDK, provider-configurable). Users select an admin-managed persona (tagged to one of the 4 existing architect categories) and describe diagrams in natural language; the AI creates and edits flowchart diagrams via targeted diagram-core operations, preserving manual work. Tracked as its own epic, separate from the Mermaid-compliance roadmap (jmuir-dtu).

title: Mermaid DSL full-compliance roadmap (diagram-type by diagram-type)
description: Syntax audit against the full Mermaid language reference (https://mermaid.ai/open-source/intro/syntax-reference.html) found real gaps across every diagram-core parser, beyond what feature 002 (US5) scoped in. This epic tracks the overall roadmap; work is deliberately split into separate bounded spec-kit features (like 001/002 before it) and interspersed with unrelated feature work rather than done as one continuous push. See child issues for the per-family breakdown.
design: Canvas supports 6 of Mermaid's ~30 diagram types: flowchart, sequence, class/UML, ER, C4, architecture (cloud infra). The other ~24 (state, gantt, pie, gitGraph, mindmap, timeline, kanban, journey, quadrant, sankey, XY chart, block, packet, requirement, ZenUML, radar, treemap, venn, Ishikawa, Wardley, Cynefin, treeview, swimlanes, event modeling) are entirely unimplemented — this was an explicit 001 spec decision, not an oversight, but is included here for roadmap completeness.

title: update-agent-context.sh corrupts CLAUDE.md: deletes '- 00N-' Recent Changes bullet headers
description:
Every run of .specify/scripts/bash/update-agent-context.sh claude deletes the leading '- 00N-<feature>:' line of older Recent Changes entries while leaving their indented continuation lines in place. The orphaned text then silently attaches to the previous bullet, so CLAUDE.md reads as though one feature's description belongs to another.

Observed 3 times in one session (features 005, 006, 007). In the 007 run it removed the headers for 001, 002, 003 and 004 in a single pass.

It also appends already-present stack entries to Active Technologies as if new (e.g. 'TypeScript 5.x, Node.js 22 LTS + React 18 + Vite ... (007-project-context)'), which conflicts with the established 'No new technology added in NNN' convention used by 002/006/007.
design: Root cause not yet investigated — the script is upstream spec-kit tooling, so the fix may be a local wrapper rather than an edit to the vendored script.
acceptance_criteria: Running the script against a CLAUDE.md containing multiple Recent Changes entries leaves every '- 00N-' header intact, and adds no Active Technologies line for a stack that is already listed.
notes: Workaround in use: snapshot CLAUDE.md to the scratchpad before running, diff after, and reinstate deleted headers by hand. Verify with: grep -c '^- 00' between '## Recent Changes' and the MANUAL ADDITIONS marker.

title: Harden escapeXml in the SVG export renderer to escape apostrophes
description:
`escapeXml` in packages/diagram-core/src/render/svg-renderer.ts escapes `&`, `<`, `>` and `"`
but not `'`. Every value it currently produces is safe, so this is hardening against a future
change rather than a live defect.

WHY IT IS SAFE TODAY
Traced every call site of escapeXml in that file. Each escaped value lands in either:
  - a double-quoted attribute (data-node-id, data-container-id, data-edge-id), or
  - text content between tags.
The only single-quoted attributes in the renderer are `font-family='...'`, which interpolate
FONT_FAMILY — a module constant that never carries user input. An unescaped apostrophe cannot
break out of any of those contexts.

WHY IT IS STILL WORTH FIXING
The safety depends on a property of the *call sites*, not of the function. If anyone later
interpolates a user-controlled label into a single-quoted attribute, an apostrophe in a diagram
label becomes an attribute-injection vector in exported SVG — and exported SVG is a file users
share. Escaping `'` as `'` makes the function correct in all XML contexts and removes that
dependency on caller discipline.

HOW IT WAS FOUND
Bearer, rule javascript_lang_manual_html_sanitization (HIGH), during the security-scanning work
that added Semgrep/Bearer/Gitleaks to CI (PR #7, merged as fba160e). Bearer will keep reporting
this rule until the manual escaping is replaced or the finding is triaged away; it is currently
non-blocking, since sast-bearer only fails the build on CRITICAL.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE AT THE TIME
It changes exported bytes for any diagram label containing an apostrophe. Features 005 and 006
both deliberately kept packages/diagram-core/src/render/ untouched to preserve the
exports-match-canvas guarantee, and the security PR was scoped to adding scanners, not changing
product behaviour. This deserves to be its own change with the export tests updated alongside.
design: One-line change to escapeXml. The screen renderer (apps/web/src/canvas/shapes.tsx) needs no matching change: it builds DOM via React rather than string concatenation, so it has no escaping of its own to keep in step. Verify by exporting a diagram whose label contains an apostrophe and confirming the SVG parses and renders identically to the canvas.
acceptance_criteria: escapeXml also maps ' to '. Export-fidelity contract tests in packages/diagram-core/tests/contract/render-svg.test.ts updated for the new output, and a case added for a label containing an apostrophe. Full suite green including round-trip and export tests. Bearer re-run to confirm the HIGH finding is resolved or consciously accepted.

title: ER diagram gaps beyond feature 003: entity aliases, styling
description: After feature 003 adds attribute-block parsing, still missing: entity aliases (ENTITY [alias_name]), styling (style/classDef/class/:::), and direction (TB/BT/LR/RL).

title: Architecture diagram gaps beyond feature 003: junctions, group-to-group edges, align directive
description: After feature 003 fixes the arrowhead-edge parsing bug and preserves direction hints, still missing: junction nodes (4-way edge splits), group-to-group edges (the {group} modifier), the align row/column directive (v11.16+), and non-default icon registration syntax (iconify.design custom icons).

title: C4 diagram gaps: additional element kinds, directional Rel variants, C4Deployment, styling macros
description: Beyond feature 003's scope. Currently supports C4Context/Container/Component/Dynamic headers, Person/Person_Ext/System/System_Ext/SystemDb/Container/Container_Ext/Component/Component_Ext elements, Rel(), and System_Boundary/Container_Boundary/Enterprise_Boundary. Missing: SystemQueue/ContainerDb/ContainerQueue/ComponentDb/ComponentQueue element kinds; BiRel/Rel_Back/directional Rel_U/D/L/R; the entire C4Deployment diagram type plus Deployment_Node/Node_L/Node_R; UpdateElementStyle/UpdateRelStyle/UpdateLayoutConfig styling macros.

title: Sequence diagram gaps beyond feature 003: activation, boxes, autonumber, rect highlighting
description: After feature 003 adds notes and loop/alt/opt/par/critical/break blocks, still missing: actor keyword, participant aliases (as), create/destroy participants, box grouping, most remaining arrow types (-x, -), async open arrows, half-arrows, +/- activation shorthand and explicit activate/deactivate, rect background highlighting, autonumber, actor menu links.

title: Class diagram (UML) gaps: members/generics/annotations/namespaces/styling
description: Beyond feature 003's scope. Currently only bare 'class Foo' decl + 5 relationship arrows + optional label parse; class bodies are recognized but their contents skipped entirely (disclosed limitation in packages/diagram-core/src/dsl/uml.ts). Missing: member/attribute modeling with visibility markers (+/-/#/~), generics (~T~), cardinality/multiplicity labels on relationships, interfaces (lollipop syntax), <<annotations>> (Interface/Abstract/Service/Enumeration), notes, namespaces, styling (style/classDef/cssClass/:::), direction.

title: Mermaid flowchart parser: broader grammar coverage beyond 002's scope
description:
Feature 002 (User Story 5) added graph/flowchart alias support, %% comments, inline node-shape-in-edge declarations, and style fill/stroke directives — a bounded, prioritized subset, not full Mermaid grammar coverage (explicitly scoped down during specify, see specs/002-editing-lifecycle-enhancements/spec.md Assumptions). Not-yet-supported: other style properties (stroke-width, color, etc. beyond fill/stroke — currently parsed but ignored), classDef/class assignment, linkStyle, click interactions, subgraph direction overrides, multi-line node labels with
. File specific sub-issues if/when a real diagram import hits one of these.

title: Diagram physical purge after retention window
description: Soft-deleted diagrams past DIAGRAM_RETENTION_DAYS (30) are currently just excluded from queries via deleted_at IS NULL filters and blocked from restore (DiagramRetentionExpiredError) once expired — no job ever physically deletes the rows. Documented as a deferred concern in specs/002-editing-lifecycle-enhancements/research.md. Needs a housekeeping job/script (deliberately not built in 002 to avoid introducing a scheduler per Constitution VI simplicity).

title: Entirely unsupported Mermaid diagram types (~24, not yet scoped)
description: 001 spec explicitly deferred these; listed here for full-roadmap visibility, not yet prioritized or broken into individual features. Full list from the Mermaid syntax reference: swimlanes, state diagram, user journey, gantt, pie chart, quadrant chart, requirement diagram, gitGraph, mindmap, timeline, ZenUML, sankey, XY chart, block diagram, packet, kanban, radar, event modeling, treemap, venn, Ishikawa, Wardley, Cynefin, treeview. Split into individual per-type issues once/if prioritized — state diagram and gantt are probably the highest-value candidates given how commonly they appear in real documentation.
